notes:
SYNTHETIC FIXTURE. Halewater Commons Trust, Kelverton, Marlpit, Dunmore Sixth Form College, Second Chances, the Wren Hill Foundation and the Neighbourhood Futures Fund do not exist. Every fact in the proposal traces to an item in ledger-n03.json (3 named referents: Marlpit, Dunmore Sixth Form College, Second Chances).

WORD COUNTS, all deterministic, none from a model. wc -w on the whole file = 1605. The worker's own wordCount() (index.ts:555, strips |#*`> then counts alphanumeric tokens) = 1523. The donor counts only the five answers and explicitly excludes headings, the budget table and the declaration; counted that way the document is 1189 words against the 1200 hard limit, i.e. compliant with 11 words to spare.

STAGES RUN: analyze; org (no model call - the fixture domain must not be crawled, so the supplied ledger IS the org stage output; org.profile and org.voice_guide were left null, so baseCtx segments 2 and 6 were absent); voice (skipped, no uploads); strategy (one lost call at effort=high, then a retry); design + 1 continuation; gen:narrative + 1 continuation; generateValidated attempt-2 repair + 1 continuation; generateValidated attempt-3 shorten; validate.claim_ledger; validate.review; validate.correction + 1 continuation; validate round-1 grounding re-audit; check (skipped, nothing to compare against on a single replay); package/deliver (deterministic, not replayed).

FIDELITY DEVIATIONS, all forced and all recorded. (1) The MCP transport hard-caps a single call at 60s. The spec's max_tokens (strategy 4500, design 6000, narrative 7000, correction 7000) could not be used; nothing above ~3000 completion tokens returns in time. The strategy stage was attempted once at the spec's effort='high' with max_tokens 4500 and timed out; that call is counted in `calls` and its completion estimated at 4500 tokens because it very likely completed and was billed upstream. Every other token figure is the exact usage the API reported. Cost excluding the lost call is $1.0569. Strategy and design therefore ran at effort='low' rather than the spec's 'high'. (2) Four stages truncated on the token cap and were completed with the spec's own CONTINUATION_TURN (index.ts:154-167), but through a single-user-message transport the continuation cannot carry the original message array. The damage is visible in the design stage: the continuation abandoned the required schema entirely, emitting `budget`, `monitoring`, `assumptions` (as bare strings) and `eligibility_fit` instead of the specified `indicators`, `budget_envelope_usd`, `budget_drivers`, typed `assumptions` and `logic_check`. jsonOf() would have parsed it and the missing keys would have passed silently. (3) One departure from strict fidelity: the claim-ledger call marked 'the young people below are already known to us by name' as unsupported but material:false, so the worker's groundingProblems filter would have left it in the shipped document. It was added to the fixList and removed, because this task forbids asserting anything not in the ledger. A faithful worker run ships that sentence.

THE PIPELINE WOULD NOT HAVE DELIVERED THIS. Two separate throws. (a) gen:narrative. Attempt 1 = 1688 worker-words (violations: over_word_limit, missing_required_section:One-page budget table). Attempt 2 repair = 1483 worker-words, required section fixed, still over. Attempt 3 is the pure-shortening call, which asked for at most 936 words and returned the document essentially unchanged - it deleted the word 'already' from one sentence and three words from one table cell, then ran into the token cap. Third check still fails, so generateValidated throws 'content validation failed: over_word_limit'. This reproduces the same attempt-3 failure mode recorded in the ukyouth run, on a different case and a different word limit. (b) validate. Round 0 found 4 blocking material unsupported claims and 2 missing mandatory requirements, so the correction pass ran. The corrected narrative answered the deadline requirement but never addressed the Round 3 priorities requirement, and the round-1 grounding re-audit returned 13 further material unsupported claims. blocking > 0 at round === maxRounds, so validate throws 'validation unresolved after 1 rounds'. The order lands in attention and, per P0-4, nobody is emailed. The shipped file is the last complete document the chain produced, not one the deployed worker would have delivered.

THE WORD-LIMIT COUNTER IS THE MOST EXPENSIVE BUG IN THIS RUN, AND IT IS WORSE HERE THAN IN THE UKYOUTH CASE. contentViolations (index.ts:608) runs wordCount() over the ENTIRE markdown document. This donor states in terms that headings, the budget table and the declaration are excluded from its 1,200-word limit, and analyze correctly recorded max_words 1200 - but nothing downstream knows about the exclusion. The shipped document is 1189 donor-counted words (compliant) and 1523 worker-counted words (a violation). The attempt-3 shortener was ordered to cut to 936 total words; had it complied, the five answers would have landed somewhere near 700 donor-counted words, surrendering roughly 40 per cent of the donor's allowance on a limit the document was not breaking. The shortener's refusal to shorten is the only reason this document is still the right length.

A SECOND, SEPARATE INCONSISTENCY THE RUN EXPOSED. analyze emitted two different section lists for the same donor: application_structure.sections_or_questions ends 'Budget table (one page)', 'Declaration', while format_spec.required_sections ends 'One-page budget table', 'Declaration'. gen:narrative's donorStructure block is built from the first list; contentViolations' missing_required_section check and constraintsAt() use the second. The narrative obediently wrote '## Budget table (one page)' as instructed and was then failed for missing 'One-page budget table'. One model call was spent fixing a heading the same stage had told it to write.

THE OPENING DEVICE FIRED THIS TIME. strategy locked template 1 (problem_first) and opening device 1 (incident), 'A dated, real event that makes the problem concrete'. In the ukyouth run that instruction contradicted FACT_RULES because the ledger held no events. Here it does not: E-WEB-2 and E-WEB-3 carry dated results, and Q2 opens on 'In 2024-25 the Trust referred 27 young people... Eighteen enrolled; nine did not.' That is a real opening on real evidence. Three referents were enough to make one of the eight opening devices usable.

WHAT THE THREE REFERENTS BOUGHT, MEASURED. The proposal names Marlpit (a ward, with a census statistic and a riverbank), Dunmore Sixth Form College (a named next-step provider with a route dated to 2023 and a 27/18 conversion) and Second Chances (a dated course with 24/19/11). The donor weights 'work rooted in a named place' at 25 per cent and 'capability evidenced by what it has already done' at 20 per cent, and both are answerable here in a way they were not with a two-fact ledger. But the ceiling is visible: the proposal has no street, no venue name, no named person, no vendor and no partner beyond the college, so Q1's 'who else operates there' is unanswered and Q3's partners are 'local schools' and 'employers and apprenticeship providers' in the abstract - exactly the unnamed-geography failure the guidance says assessors treat as a gap in the plan.

GROUNDING PRESSURE IS NOW THE BINDING CONSTRAINT, NOT EVIDENCE POVERTY. The round-1 audit flagged as unsupported a set of claims the proposal arguably needs in order to exist at all: that the Trust has trustees, that it has premises in Marlpit, that its youth staff can deliver a twelve-week course (though E-WEB-3 says it ran one), that its advice desk serves Marlpit rather than the east side generally, and that its referral process is currently informal. Several of those readings are too strict, and the budget figures it flagged are future design, not past fact. But the pipeline cannot tell an over-strict audit from a correct one: blocking is a count, and 13 blocking claims throws the stage regardless. The correction pass also has no way to satisfy 'address at least two Round 3 priorities' without adding words to a document it has just been told must not get longer, so it silently dropped that finding. Both failure modes are structural, not model-quality.

COST OF PADDING. The design landed at GBP 74,928 against a GBP 75,000 ceiling: 72 pounds of headroom, after a design prompt that says in terms 'if the design naturally costs far less than the ceiling, keep it lower - never pad'. The deterministic ceiling guard could not catch it because the grant is denominated in GBP and analyze correctly returned funding_ceiling_usd null, so budget_envelope_usd was never compared to anything. That is P2-10 with the same second edge found in the ukyouth run: the guard silently does not run for any non-USD grant. On a criterion weighted 15 per cent for value for money, GBP 74,928 for 33 confirmed six-week retentions is GBP 2,271 each, and no cost-per-participant figure appears anywhere in the document.

HONEST VERDICT ON THE ARTEFACT. It is a competent, specific, internally consistent application. The causal chain holds: four named causes, each mapped to an activity, each activity with months, deliverer and venue; a measurement chain from 70 caseload to 33 in place at six weeks against a real 27/18 baseline; a failure threshold declared in advance; and a sustainability answer that says plainly no future funder is secured and the keyworker post does not continue. The budget arithmetic is exact (66,900 direct, 8,028 overhead at precisely the 12 per cent cap, 74,928). Against the donor's own weights the weaknesses are: the Round 3 priorities are never named, no partner or venue beyond the college is identified, and value for money is asserted rather than shown. It reads as written by someone who knows the ward. It does not read as machine-generated, which the two-fact ukyouth ledger could not achieve.
